title: Nvidia Stock News (Oct 16, 2026): NVDA Falls 1.8% to $217.23
summary: Nvidia (NVDA) fell 1.84% to $217.23 on Oct 15, 2026, lagging a slightly higher Nasdaq as pressure on AI infrastructure stocks carried on.
body_markdown:
## Why Nvidia Stock Fell


None of the sources fetched for this article named a company-specific cause for Nvidia's decline, and no new Nvidia release or filing tied to the session was found. The move is best read against the indices and peers above, with Nvidia lagging a market that closed higher.


The backdrop for Nvidia-linked names was weak. As reported by[TheStreet](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/deutsche-bank-blunt-advice-nvidia-215000653.html) , CoreWeave, which rents out computing power built on Nvidia chips to AI developers, fell more than 15% on October 14 to close at $65.78 and slid about 6% further in premarket trading on October 15.


The same report said yields on CoreWeave bonds due 2031 rose above 16% and that chip stocks in the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index had lost substantial market value over six sessions.


Per TheStreet, Reuters reported that CoreWeave is loss-making and carries about $50 billion in debt, which has put the financing behind AI data center buildouts in focus for investors in the chip supply chain.


## NVDA Stock Analysis: Supporting Factors and Risks


### Supporting Factors


- According to[Motley Fool](https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/not-nvidia-not-cisco-ai-233500002.html) , Nvidia is the world's largest company, largely because of GPUs the outlet describes as essential for training and running AI models.
- The same Motley Fool report put Nvidia's gain so far this year at about 20%, and the stock still carries a market capitalization of $5.33 trillion after the session.
- The stock closed 32.24% above its 52-week low of $164.27 and finished $4.38 above the day's low.


### Risks


- Debt stress at CoreWeave, a customer that builds on Nvidia chips, keeps pressure on AI infrastructure stocks, per TheStreet.
- Chip stocks in the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index shed substantial market value over six sessions, according to TheStreet, a sign of sector-wide selling.
- Nvidia lagged the Nasdaq Composite by 1.92 percentage points on above-average volume and sits 10.74% below its 52-week high.
